pattern-selector.why: the subagent coverage is a deliberate record-plus-gate split: a per-session ledger written by the edit-gate and the subagent-check, read by the parent as a backstop, with per-file coverage; the shared transcript parser was extracted rather than copied. The forces and the rejected alternatives (reuse finish-check unchanged; record only at hand-back) are in ADR-0102.
pattern-selector.what: built the SubagentStop hand-back check and the ledger-backed parent backstop; recorded the design and its alternatives in ADR-0102.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

architectural-decision-records.why: holding subagents to the formula and the parent backstop are a significant decision; the choice, the alternatives, and the honest not-assessed limits are recorded in the same change.
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0102 (subagents held to the formula: hand-back check, parent backstop, preloaded skills).
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the subagent behaviors are specified as executable scenarios across the subagent and operator audiences and happy/negative/edge/error/concurrency/timeout/adverse paths, tagged, logged, and reconciled against the datastore.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added 13 scenarios (2 to the formula feature, 11 in a new subagents-apply-skills.feature) and a step file driving the real subagent-check, parent finish-check, plan check, claim-lint and router; the chain is green at 95 scenarios.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the parser, the hand-back check, and the downgrade are proven at the lowest level that catches the bug: unit tests that spawn the real scripts or call the pure functions with crafted inputs.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added test/subagent-check.test.mjs, test/transcript-files.test.mjs, test/subagent-claim.test.mjs, and parent-backstop/edit-gate-ledger additions; wired them into the test list.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the subagent-check is a gate, so every block/flag/downgrade branch carries a test that fails when it is neutralized: no-receipt, named-but-unread, reviewer-no-evidence, unreadable transcript, parent per-file over-clear, main-vs-subagent ledger, and the idempotent downgrade.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: wrote discriminating tests that flip when each branch is neutralized, including the per-file coverage and scoped-named-skill fixes from the review.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

skeptical-audit.why: the honest limits are stated, not hidden (SubagentStop/agent_transcript_path/skills-frontmatter not-assessed, the backstop's agent-id dependence, the named-skill scoping and its fail-open, the no-transcript escape), and the parent is made to NOT launder a subagent's 'verified' claim unless it re-ran it.
skeptical-audit.what: built the parent claim-downgrade and disclosed every limit in ADR-0102.
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: a fresh-context review of the whole change ran against the four questions and raised 5 findings (2 medium, 3 low), all fixed before the PR and recorded in the append-only review log.
judge-arch.what: ran judge-arch in fresh context, fixed every finding (named-skill scoping, per-file coverage, idempotent banner, not-wired order, static import), and appended the review entry.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

release-deployment-safety.why: SubagentStop now registers subagent-check in place of finish-check, a change to what runs; it ships behind the opt-in --enforce, the wiring is idempotent and additive, and an install-time canary runs the new script before it goes live - deploy kept apart from release.
release-deployment-safety.what: swapped the SubagentStop registration and extended the enforcement canary to cover subagent-check in esk-init.mjs.
quotes: Dark-launch: ship the code off, turn it on for internal users, then 1 percent

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: transcript parsing is kept in one owner (transcript-files.mjs) rather than copied into each hook, and the parent coverage is the simpler per-file rule that meets the requirement; the simpler shape was chosen on purpose.
enterprise-architecture-standards.what: extracted the shared transcript parser and had finish-check import it; made parent coverage per file.
quotes: Simplicity that meets the real requirement is a core principle, not a shortcut.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: the change touches input handling (the brief and the subagent transcript are parsed into a decision) and a security-relevant flow (a subagent changing how a secret value is masked must have a threat model before it can hand back). The named-skill match is hardened to scope to the brief's Skills block with word boundaries so injected skill-list text cannot force a false over-block, and the secret-masking control ships a @security scenario in the shared feature index.
owasp-secure-coding-bdd.what: hardened the named-skill match against injected brief text and added the @security subagent-skips-plan scenario (a secret-masking change with no threat model cannot hand back), driven through the real plan check.
quotes: Each per-sheet file states the real attack the control stops

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: the subagent ledger holds operational data (agent names, changed-file paths, a receipt flag), not personal or regulated data, so there is no data class, retention, or deletion duty in this change.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service or endpoint is added; the hand-back check and backstop are hooks, covered by their tests, not by SLIs/alerts/runbooks.

arch-encode.why: no greppable mistake was caught that needs a new arch-gate forbid rule; the review findings were fixed in code and pinned by discriminating tests.

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no user interface; the only human-facing output is plain-text agent-facing messages and a SessionStart context string.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser or device surface; these are Node hooks, an installer, and agent-definition docs.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no end-user UI; the brief template and the hand-back messages are written in plain language naming the missing item and its fix, but there is no interactive surface to design.
